verdict: Avoid new steel re-rolling/TMT exposure in Byrnihat until pollution-compliance status and GST-linked demand are verified; lend only to compliant, branded, backward-integrated units with tight structure.
title: Byrnihat steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A Byrnihat re-roller buys sponge iron, scrap and billets, melts and rolls them into TMT bars, and sells to builders, dealers and government contractors. **Cash is made on the spread between input cost and TMT realisation, not on volume alone.** The town sits on the Assam-Meghalaya border and hosts a dense cluster of factories; Frontline reports unchecked expansion has poisoned air and water, and cites the IQAir 2024 report calling Byrnihat the world's most polluted metropolitan area with PM2.5 of 128.2 micrograms per cubic metre against a WHO guideline of 5 [2]. **That environmental load is now a credit fact, not a CSR issue.**

## What has changed now
In July 2026 the Meghalaya High Court criticised the state pollution board for ignoring a March report on Byrnihat air quality and demanded urgent action [1]. **Regulatory action can stop a furnace, and a stopped furnace still services debt.** Meghalaya GST collections are down 14.8% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D] — a local demand signal that sits badly with a re-roller's dependence on state construction. Brent at $113/bbl is above the $75–100 band [D], which raises power and freight cost for a rolling mill. **So when a proposal lands, check the unit's consent-to-operate validity and any pollution-board notice; if consent is expired or under challenge, ask for the compliance plan and stop.**

## Where the growth is
Peer results show the TMT market itself is not dead: Steel Exchange India clocked ~₹340 crore revenue in Q2 FY27, up ~45% YoY [6], and Rathi Steel & Power reported over ₹200 crore, up over 30% YoY with volume growth of ~28.86% [7]. JSW Steel's Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 20% [5]. **Pursue branded TMT makers with dealer networks and backward integration into billets; avoid pure job-work rollers with no brand and no captive power.** Rating reports flag that sudden input-price swings hit margins [10] and that working capital needs are moderately high [11] — so structure limits against inventory and receivables, not against hope.

## How to grow safely
Take monthly stock and receivable statements, GST returns, and electricity bills — power draw is the cleanest proxy for actual rolling days. **Set the drawing power on a stock-and-book-debt basis and covenant a minimum interest coverage and a cap on gearing; Kubair's gearing moved to 1.80x from 1.40x on debt-funded acquisition and higher working capital borrowings [10].** Ask for the pollution-board consent renewal date and the unit's captive power share; collect from customer where these are not on file.

## Early-warning signs
- Monthly GST filed vs stock statement mismatch (monthly) -> freeze limit and inspect godown.
- Electricity units consumed falling while sales reported flat (monthly) -> ask for production log and re-rate.
- Pollution-board notice or consent lapse (event-based) -> stop disbursement until clearance.
- Receivable days stretching beyond sanctioned cycle (monthly) -> shift to cash-backed sales.
